title: Free amino-acid content of perennial ryegrass plant parts at defoliation
source_location: Publisher abstract; free-amino-acid contents reported for stubble, leaves, and roots on the day of defoliation
geography: Experiment location not stated in the accessible abstract; author affiliation is not treated as experiment location
material: Perennial ryegrass (Lolium perenne L.), separated into leaves, stubble, and roots
measurement_method: The article studies nitrogen remobilization and free amino-acid composition/content; method details are in the full article and are not inferred from the abstract extract.
evidence_class: Primary literature measurements; class B for source observations
license: Publisher access terms apply. This repository extract contains three abstract-reported numeric facts and provenance, not article text or figures; verify reuse rights before redistribution.
activation_state: Reference-only. Not connected to the GreenHub active composition because the source reports plant parts rather than matched Dutch roadside whole grass and does not resolve overlap with total-N-derived protein.
limitations: The material is cultivated perennial ryegrass, not the project VARTA roadside-grass sample.
The three values are plant-part-specific and cannot be aggregated without plant-part mass fractions.
The accessible abstract does not report sample count, variance, or a GreenHub-matched analytical basis beyond dry weight.
Free amino acids contain nitrogen and may overlap with crude-protein values derived from total nitrogen; no active profile conversion was made.
